primary_diagnosis_treated: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease – post-MI secondary-prevention
nice_guideline_used: CG126/NG185 (secondary prevention after MI), NG106 (chronic heart failure disease-modifying therapy)

medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of cardiovascular events after MI
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126/NG185 recommends lifelong low‑dose aspirin for all patients with established IHD

medications.dose: 80 mg orally once daily in the evening
medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce non‑HDL‑C by ≥40% and lower risk of recurrent MI
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126/NG185 recommends high‑intensity statin for all patients with IHD

medications.dose: Start 2.5 mg orally once daily; titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5‑10 mg daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function and potassium after each titration, then annually
medications.purpose: Cardioprotective antihypertensive; improves survival post‑MI and in HF
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126/NG185 and NG106 list ACE‑I as first‑line disease‑modifying therapy for post‑MI and HFrEF

medications.dose: Start 1.25 mg orally once daily; titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5‑10 mg daily aiming HR <70 bpm
medications.duration: Lifelong — review heart rate, blood pressure and glucose after each titration, then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce myocardial oxygen demand, improve survival after MI and in HF
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126/NG185 and NG106 recommend beta‑blocker as first‑line post‑MI and HF therapy

medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce cardiovascular mortality and heart‑failure hospitalisation; renal protection
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 (TA902/TA929) recommends SGLT2‑i for all patients with HFrEF regardless of diabetes status

interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP and symptoms of hypotension after each dose change

interactions_checked.interaction: Both can affect renal function; risk of AKI if volume depleted
interactions_checked.action: Ensure adequate hydration; monitor creatinine/eGFR after initiation

contraindications.reason: Negative inotrope that worsens heart failure (NG106 contraindicated)
Can worsen renal function and cause fluid retention in CKD/HF (NG106)
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol or topical agents for pain

contraindications.reason: Fluid retention risk in HF and CKD (NG106)
Dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalaemia and renal injury (guideline rule)
contraindications.alternative: Only add ARB if ACE‑I intolerant

assumptions_warnings: LVEF not recorded – assumed no HFrEF; MRA (spironolactone) withheld until echocardiogram confirms LVEF ≤40%
Baseline serum potassium not available – will obtain before ACE‑I titration and monitor after each change
Blood pressure reading not provided – assume uncontrolled hypertension; will measure at each visit
Allergy status unknown – will verify aspirin, ACE‑I, and statin tolerance before prescribing
Discrepancy between creatinine (3.0 mg/dL) and eGFR (81.9 mL/min) – will repeat renal panel to confirm true renal function before ACE‑I and SGLT2‑i initiation
treatment_summary: Start lifelong low‑dose aspirin, high‑intensity atorvastatin, ramipril and bisoprolol with careful titration, and dapagliflozin for secondary cardiovascular prevention and heart‑failure benefit. Avoid drugs that worsen HF or renal function (verapamil, diltiazem, NSAIDs, pioglitazone, class I antiarrhythmics) and do not combine ACE‑I with an ARB. Monitor BP, heart rate, renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes and lipids per NICE guidance, and arrange echocardiography to determine need for additional HF therapies.
